proof:
Put $C'=2y-C$ and $J=|A\cap C'|$. For each nonvertical cap through $(0,y)$, the calculation of pk-w35-reflected-discrepancy gives traces on $A,C'$ that are closed opposite ordinary halfspaces. Their masses from the common intersection sum to $J$ since its hyperplane slice is Lebesgue-null. Pure base caps take at least $a\ge J$. This gives the lower bound, and $A\subset C'$ implies $p(y)=a$ by the pure base upper bound.

Conversely, if $p(y)=a$, the discrepancy identity gives $\Delta=b-a$. The signed values $v(H)=|C'\cap H|-|A\cap H|$ and their opposite values $b-a-v(H)$ are both at most $\Delta$. Thus $v(H)\ge0$ for every $H$. If a point of $A$ were outside $C'$, strict separation from the compact convex $C'$ would give a closed halfspace disjoint from $C'$ with that point in its interior. The halfspace contains a point of $\operatorname{int}A$, by taking nearby convex combinations with an interior point of $A$, so it has positive $A$-volume. This contradicts $v(H)\ge0$. Reflecting $A\subset C'$ gives $2y-A\subset C$, and the displayed erosion is convex by the convexity of $C$. For intervals, align their midpoints. For equal volumes, proper containment of one full-dimensional compact convex body in the other would produce a strict positive volume difference by the same separation argument. Thus containment forces equality, which is precisely the stated reflection and translation condition.
statement: Let $A,C\subset\mathbb R^d$ be full-dimensional compact convex bodies with $0<a=|A|\le b=|C|$, $d\ge1$. For their two unnormalized volume layers at $-1,1$, let $p(y)$ be raw closed ambient halfspace depth at $(0,y)$. For every $y$, $p(y)\ge |A\cap(2y-C)|$ and $p(y)=a$ if and only if $2y-A\subset C$. The depth-$a$ region is the convex set $\tfrac12\{t:t-A\subset C\}$. It is nonempty for intervals and, for equal-volume convex bodies, nonempty exactly when $C$ is a translate of $-A$.
title: Reflected containment characterizes the full smaller-layer depth
